name: Cessna 310
summary: Five-to-six-seat light piston twin and Cessna's first postwar twin, recognisable by its wingtip fuel tanks.

wings: Low straight wing with fuel tanks on the wingtips
Engines mounted on the wing close to the fuselage
engines: Two flat-six engines in slim nacelles that extend well behind the wing
fuselage: Slim five-to-six-seat cabin with large side windows
Long pointed nose on later models
tail: Swept fin with dorsal fillet (straight-edged fin on early models)

tellTales: Low-wing piston twin with fuel tanks on the wingtips
Long pointed nose and swept fin
Slim nacelles extending behind the wing trailing edge

confusedWith.howToTell: The Baron has plain wingtips with no tip tanks; the 310 has prominent wingtip tanks.
The 340/414/421 have a fatter cabin-class fuselage with small rounded windows; the 310 is slimmer with large rectangular windows.
The Aztec has a boxy slab-sided fuselage, a thick constant-chord wing and plain wingtips; the 310 is sleeker with tip tanks.
The 402 is a bigger, longer-cabin twin seating six to ten; the 310 is smaller and slimmer.
